v: You know you are watching a GREAT movie when even Chunky Panday gets a scary, meaty role! Bold emotions, rustic dialogues, top-notch BGM and terrific performances — and Vidya is every bit Bollywood’s BEGUM JAAN.
e: Begum Jaan worked for me through sheer emotional force rather than conventional action. The rustic writing, excellent performances and powerful music create goosebumps without needing elaborate stunt sequences, while Vidya Balan dominates the centre and even Chunky Panday becomes genuinely frightening. Its boldness may limit the family audience, but the impact is undeniable.
body:
You know you are watching a GREAT movie when even Chunky Panday gets a meaty role and turns genuinely scary as Kabir!!!!!

And what a superb movie this is — full of bold emotions, rustic dialogues, top-notch BGM and excellent acting from practically every artist 🙏

You do not need giant stunts or elaborate action episodes to create goosebumps.

Sometimes all it takes is a great dialogue delivered at the right moment and music that knows exactly when to hit.

Begum Jaan repeatedly proves that.

And man… if Kangana is called the Queen of Bollywood, then Vidya Balan is absolutely her BEGUM JAAN!!!!!

I am not sure how commercially successful a film with this kind of bold content can be, especially when the so-called family audience may stay away.

But irrespective of box office, this movie is going to leave an impact on the people who watch it.

P.S. I had not watched the original Bengali version, so I was judging this film completely on its own.

v: Buy one movie ticket and somehow THREE movies come searching for you 😄 Srinu Vaitla’s multithreading obsession turns a 2h40m film into a 10-hour experience, complete with three climaxes and character-artist employment for everyone.
e: Mister left me wondering how Varun Tej agreed to the film and convinced that Srinu Vaitla had not escaped the formula he was expected to change. Characters and subplots keep arriving without purpose, the second half becomes exhausting and the climax itself seems to multiply — a sprawling commercial mess rather than a coherent entertainer.
body:
The official tagline says something like: if we go searching for love, love will come searching for us.

For me, Mister needed a more accurate tagline: buy a ticket for one movie and somehow THREE movies will come searching for you!!!!! 😄

I genuinely could not understand how Varun Tej agreed to this script.

I went in hoping Srinu Vaitla might finally have changed his familiar formula.

I came out with the much stronger belief that manam chachinaa eeyana maaradu 😄

Half the time I could not understand why so many characters were entering, what they were supposed to do, or what Vaitla himself planned to make them do.

It almost feels like a giant employment scheme for Telugu character artists 🙏

The Krishnadevaraya-family stretch in the second half is especially exhausting.

A movie that runs around two hours and forty minutes somehow creates the feeling that you have been sitting there for ten hours.

And just when you start desperately waiting for the climax… you get THREE climaxes and fresh tears of blood 😄

I suspect Srinu Vaitla developed a childhood fascination with the Java multithreading concept and has been faithfully applying the same architecture to his screenplays movie after movie.

v: Keep expectations underground, ignore the story, close your eyes for Shruti and somehow close both eyes AND ears for the songs… then maybe 😄 PK is the only real saving grace in a film that feels cheaply assembled around him.
e: Katamarayudu felt like a storyline that belonged in the 2000s filmed with visual effects from the 1990s. Pawan Kalyan’s screen presence and Ajay’s expressions are almost the only positives I found, while the music, BGM, supporting material and exaggerated performance choices make the entire package feel surprisingly cheap for a star vehicle.
body:
If you have been watching all the out-of-the-box films arriving around this period, then Katamarayudu comes with a few viewing instructions 😄

Do not expect too much.

Do not think too deeply about the story.

Close your eyes whenever required… and when the songs arrive, somehow find a way to close your ears along with them.

If you can manage all that, perhaps the movie becomes easier to survive 😄

This feels like a storyline that should have been made in the 2000s with CG work that looks as though it came from the 1990s.

The only real saving grace is Power Star Pawan Kalyan, supported in places by Ajay’s expressions.

The most irritating parts for me are Anup Rubens’ music and BGM, amplified further by Shruti Haasan’s exaggerated performance.

Apart from the “Oka Rayudoooo” BGM bit, I found the music horrible.

At this rate, Anup may have to wait another ten years before somebody hands him another huge star-hero film 😄

My bigger frustration is that the makers seem to think putting PK in the centre is enough.

Then the story, supporting cast, music and even Shruti’s styling can apparently be bought cheaply from the local market 🙏

For a film built around such a massive star, that surrounding carelessness is impossible to ignore.

v: An excellent, still-relevant plot about dowry and women’s independence gets trapped inside confused commercial treatment. Neither a strong issue-driven film nor a satisfying entertainer — and seriously, shouldn’t this have been Vaidehi Ka Dulha? 😄
e: Badrinath Ki Dulhania starts from themes I found worthwhile and realistic, especially dowry and the expectations placed on women. Varun Dhawan does justice to the Jhansi tapori and Alia Bhatt is effortless, but the commercial packaging repeatedly weakens the material until the film sits awkwardly between social drama and mainstream entertainer without fully succeeding as either.
body:
I normally start by talking about the good points of a movie, but here I could not hold myself back from laughing at one irony.

The entire plot revolves around women’s empowerment and opposition to dowry.

Varun’s character gradually becomes a better man under the influence of Alia’s character.

So why exactly is the movie called Badrinath Ki Dulhania?

Vaidehi Ka Dulha would have been a far more appropriate title 😄

These may look like small things, but they also show how deeply male-dominated our industry remains even while using words such as “women empowerment” for preaching.

Way to go, Dharma Productions and KJo 🙏

The actual story deals with dowry and women’s independence.

Some viewers may say the theme or screenplay feels like something from the 1990s, but unfortunately these issues still exist in many Indian families.

So full credit to Varun Dhawan for choosing the subject.

He does justice to the good-hearted Jhansi tapori, while the role is almost a cakewalk for Alia — nothing here really challenges the full potential of that little dynamite.

My problem is that the plot is excellent but the completely commercial treatment becomes the spoilsport.

At the end, you neither feel you watched a great story-driven movie nor a proper commercial entertainer.

If you watch it for the realistic issue, the way the film treats it can feel frustrating.

If you watch it purely as commercial entertainment, the serious storyline starts feeling awkward inside that packaging.

It gets trapped between its two intentions.
